 Binary Predicate Symbol (Kernel Primitive) Class × Class → Bool | Class.Expression × Class.Expression → Fm [Primitive / Undefinable] Natural-Language Definition: The fundamental undefinable binary relation of class theory, read “class x is a member (element) of class Y”. Because it is the primitive membership relation at the root of the ontology, it is not defined in terms of prior notions; instead, it is governed by Class Comprehension (RulClassComprehension (3.01) / AxmMetaClassComprehension (4.06)), Sethood (DefIsSet (3.02): x set ⟷ ∃(Y:Class)(x ∈ Y), i.e., only sets can be members of classes), and Extensionality (AxmExtensionality (3.10)). Never used for typing (use :).  Kernel Quotation & Antiquotation Operators (Primitive) A → A.Expression | A.Expression → A [Primitive / Undefinable Reflection Operators] Natural-Language Definition: Explicit syntax quotation ‹e› suspends evaluation of an expression e:A and returns its syntactic AST object of type A.Expression (e.g., ‹𝛗› : Fm = Bool.Expression).  Kernel Syntactic Hygiene Symbols (Primitive) A.Expression → Class | A.Expression × Variable × Fm → Bool [Primitive Syntactic Hygiene Operators] Natural-Language Definition: FV(e:A.Expression) returns the class of encoded free variables occurring unbound in syntactic expression e (strictly requiring .Expression sort such as Fm or Class.Expression, never semantic Bool). FFI((t:X.Expression),x,(𝛗:Fm)) holds iff no free variable of t becomes captured when substituted for free occurrences of x in 𝛗. NFV(X,x,(𝛃:Fm)) asserts that x:X does not occur free in 𝛃:Fm.
